problem:
Solve the initial value problem

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

given that the general solution to our differential equation is

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

The solution to the initial value problem is

| $x(t)=\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} |  | $\,\,{e}^{t}+\,\,$ |  | {{field-2}} |  | $\,\,{e}^{-t}.$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-3}} |  |  | {{field-4}} |  |  |  |  |
worked_solution:
To find the values of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$, we substitute $t=0$ in the general solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(0) & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]{e}^{0}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{0} & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}2{c}_{1}+{c}_{2} \\ -{c}_{1}+{c}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{c}_{1}+{c}_{2}=7 \\ -{c}_{1}+{c}_{2}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying the second equation by $2$ and adding the result to the  first equation, we get

$$
3{c}_{2}=9\,⟹\,{c}_{2}=3.
$$

Substituting this into the second equation, we obtain 

$$
-{c}_{1}+3=1\,⟹\,{c}_{1}=2.
$$

 
Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =2\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+3\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}.\end{aligned}
$$
